📖 How to use

  1. Choose decimal → BCD or BCD → decimal.
  2. For decimal → BCD pick packed (two digits per byte) or unpacked (one nibble per digit) display.
  3. Press Convert to see each digit as a 4-bit nibble plus the byte/hex view.
  4. For BCD → decimal, paste nibbles like 1001 0011 and get the decoded number.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is BCD?

Binary-Coded Decimal encodes each decimal digit in its own 4-bit nibble (0→0000 … 9→1001). Packed BCD stores two digits per byte; unpacked BCD uses one byte per digit.

Why use BCD instead of binary?

BCD avoids binary↔decimal rounding surprises, so it is used in financial systems, digital clocks and seven-segment display drivers where exact decimal digits matter.

Which nibbles are invalid in BCD?

1010 through 1111 (A–F) are not valid BCD digits. The decoder rejects them and tells you exactly which nibble is bad.
